content: <thought>We have measured the mass spectrum of the unknown sample. The most intense peak is at m/z 121.0528, with an M+1 peak at 122.0559 (≈8 % of the base peak) and a very small M+2 peak at 123.0581. The relative intensity of the M+1 peak suggests the molecule contains roughly 7–8 carbon atoms (each ¹³C contributes ~1 % to the M+1 peak). Therefore the molecular formula is likely C₈H₉O (exact monoisotopic mass 121.0653) or a close isomer such as C₆H₅N₂O (exact mass 121.0401). To discriminate between these possibilities we need NMR data. The next inexpensive experiment is a ¹H NMR spectrum, which will reveal the number and type of hydrogen environments and help confirm the presence or absence of heteroatoms like nitrogen.
